A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VIRO research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original VIRO benchmark results, verification ablations, runtime measurements, and qualitative experiments in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original VIRO experiments and adds GQA results, additional backbone comparisons, and RefEgo validation results.

M1.justification: Appendix A.10 adds a bounded GQA adaptation with ASK and CROP_DIRECTION operators, implemented through Python logic and prompt registration. The core REC pipeline, verification scores, calibration, validator, and early-exit procedure remain unchanged. Corrected operator names in examples do not establish further algorithm changes.

E1.justification: v2 adds actual evaluation on GQA, extending coverage from referring-expression localization and rejection to compositional visual question answering. Existing REC datasets remain. TestB coverage already existed in v1's appendices, and the added RefEgo validation split does not constitute a new domain.

E2.justification: Qwen2.5-VL is added to the REC comparisons in Tables 2, 3, and A1. The existing compositional comparator suite remains represented, including GLIP accuracy comparisons in the appendices, although its GLIP runtime comparison rows disappear from Table 3.

E3.justification: The added experiments introduce GQA evaluation with BLIP-2, GLIP, and GPT-3.5-turbo; GPT-4o/mini REC configurations; Qwen2.5-VL prompting controls; and comparisons of fine-tuned versus zero-shot NAVER detectors. RefEgo validation evaluation is also added. These substantially extend experimental configurations without establishing changes to the retained core REC protocol.

E4.justification: v2 extends backbone sensitivity and latency analysis to GPT-4o/mini, adds a detector-controlled NAVER comparison, and reports Qwen2.5-VL's sensitivity to an explicit no-target instruction. Existing verification, threshold, CLIP, Llama, early-exit, and NAVER self-correction analyses remain largely unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. CLIP-based uncertainty verification is an algorithmic component, not statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: New results include VIRO's 45.4% GQA accuracy, 49.6% RefEgo-validation Acc@0.5+n, and 72.3% RefCOCO TestA TPR with GPT-4o. These are additional settings, not same-setting improvements. Several existing entries change: Table A5 corrects NAVER+GLIP test accuracy from 0.7/0.5 to 70.0/51.9 for Exc./Inc., matching v1's main table. GLIP compositional throughput entries are removed, while headline REC and RefEgo test results remain stable.

T1.justification: Section 4.2.3 removes v1's incorrect nonlinear-growth conclusion for a runtime expression proportional to N. This is a limited correction to mathematical reasoning; the runtime expressions, verification and calibration equations, and other formal definitions remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract changes the failure-rate claim from less than 0.3% to at most 0.3% and replaces superior throughput with efficient per-query runtime. The introduction explicitly presents identifying forced prediction as a contribution. The central verification, zero-shot grounding, and scalability claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds reasoning about explicitly enforced verification in Appendix A.1.4 and attributes the official NAVER performance gap to detector fine-tuning in A.9.1. It also qualifies VRAM comparisons by model-loading strategy and explicitly distinguishes the NAVER early-exit analysis from its default configuration.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a code repository link, the complete Qwen2.5-VL prompt and output format, and implementation information for the GQA adaptation and additional backbones. Most existing hardware, calibration, and iteration-budget details remain. The dated NAVER implementation reference becomes less specific.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for Qwen2.5-VL, GQA, and GPT-4o, removes T-Rex and Stairway to Success, and replaces the Qwen model reference. Its discussion of NAVER additionally distinguishes fine-tuned and zero-shot detector configurations. The broader related-work organization and positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: v2 polishes the abstract, contribution list, method explanations, and experimental discussion; corrects operator terminology; and adds acknowledgements. The appendix separates baseline error handling from detailed results and introduces several subsections. The main section sequence and substantial portions of the prose are retained.

P2.justification: The central comparison displays are substantially revised: Table 2 gains parallel TestA/TestB columns, and Table 3 replaces throughput with end-to-end and execution latency while changing its row structure. Figure 2 is redrawn, runtime reporting is reorganized, and new RefEgo-validation, backbone, GPT, and GQA tables are added. Existing qualitative examples are relocated and relabeled rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: v2 improves evaluation credibility through the added Qwen baseline, controlled NAVER comparisons, and corrected appendix results, while the code link and explicit prompt improve reproducibility information. The core evidence remains largely stable. Benefits outweigh limited losses, including removed GLIP timing results and the unsupported claim in Appendix A.7 that API runtime is execution-dominated despite reporting 1.06 seconds of pre-execution versus 0.71 seconds of execution.
